sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. On the basis of complaint lodged by one Mohammed Usman Sait, FIR was registered by Whitefield Police in Crime No.224/2019 against one Mahammed Wasim and 4 others.
In the said FIR, the petitioner was not arrayed as the accused.

In the complaint, it was averred that the complainant had purchased site No.41, khata No.394 (New No.432 and old No.356) situated at Gandhipura on 15.06.2013 from one Sri.Ashraf Ahmed and the revenue records of the said land also stood in the name of the complainant.

It is further alleged in NC: 2023:KHC:29477 the complaint that the accused persons named in complaint had created false documents in respect of the aforesaid site belonging to the complainant and one Sri.Mahammed Wasim claiming to be the son of the complainant had created a death certificate of the complainant and thereafter, executed a sale deed.
On the basis of the complaint dated 22.05.2019, FIR was registered initially against Mahammed Wasim and 4 others.

Apprehending arrest in the instant case, the petitioner had filed Crl.Mics.No.981/2020 before the VI Additional Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District,
Bengaluru, which was dismissed on 31.08.2020.

entities.text:
VI Additional Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District,
Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed on 05.12.2022 and in the said charge sheet, the petitioner has been arrayed as accused No.1.
It is in this background, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegation against accused Nos.1 and 2 in the charge sheet is identical and accused No.2 has been granted anticipatory bail by the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.827/2019 on 07.06.2019.

entities.text: VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner has no criminal antecedents and undisputedly, no consideration has been received by the NC: 2023:KHC:29477 petitioner from second accused Sanjay with regard to the alleged sale transaction and therefore, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the bail petition and submits that the petitioner is the person who has executed the sale deed in favour of accused No.2-Sanjay Sri.

entities.text: Rab Nawaz vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and therefore, it cannot be said that accused No.2 and the petitioner stand on the same footing.

Accordingly, she prays to dismiss the petition.
6.
In the complaint, which was lodged on 22.05.2019, it is stated that Mahammed Wasim who was arrayed as accused No.1 in the FIR had created a sale deed in favour of Sanjay.
The petitioner was not arrayed as accused in the FIR.

During the course of investigation, it was found that it was the petitioner who had registered the sale deed, in respect of the property belonging to the complainant,
in favour of Sanjay.

From the charge sheet allegation, it is seen that admittedly the petitioner has not received any sale consideration in respect of the property in question from the second accused Sanjay in whose favour the sale deed was created.

Therefore, accused NC: 2023:KHC:29477 No.1 and 2 stand on the same footing and accused No.2-Sanjay has been granted anticipatory bail by the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru in Crl.Misc.No.827/2019 on 07.06.2019.

entities.text: VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed as against the petitioner subsequently.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The respondent-Police or any other police in the state of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.224/2019 registered by Whitefield Police Station, Bengaluru city for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 420, 465, 468, 471, 120B r/w Section 34 of IPC, subject to the following conditions.

1. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this Order and shall executed a personal bond for a sum of NC: 2023:KHC:29477 Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigation Officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the trial Court without fail unless exempted by the trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness either directly or indirectly.
4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future.
Sd/-
